newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel little changed against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel little changed against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed almost unchanged against the dollar on Monday in trendless trading, dealers said.

"It's the same old story, the basket is still trading at seven percent below the diagonal rate and the Bank of Israel had to intervene again in the market buying dollars to support the basket," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.

"The dollar was stable abroad and the representative rate of the dollar was set slightly higher. Overall we saw a slight increase in the supply of foreign currency and the central bank had to raise the sum it purchased," the dealer added.
The Bank of Israel has been intervening regularly in the market to defend the currency basket rate, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for two months.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3700 shekels against 3.3690 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6491 shekels against 3.6475 on Friday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7661 shekels per 100 yen against 2.7781 on Friday and against the mark at 1.9725 shekels against 1.9644 on Friday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.3675 shekels.
